research_questions: Is ColQwen2 v0.1->v1.0 a second backbone on which a post-vision cut is legal, reproduces the target index exactly, and admits at least one compressed point under the frozen -0.01 nDCG@5 floor?

transition.processor_contract: Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct base processor as loaded by colpali_engine ColQwen2Processor (602,112 max pixels); identical for both versions by construction.

calibration: Same split as sigir-version-evolution-matrix-v1: numpy RandomState(0) reserves 30% of documents as the holdout; the first 64 sorted non-holdout documents fit one query-free PCA basis of rank 512 from 8192 uniformly sampled visual tokens. Lower ranks truncate that nested basis.

evaluation.reference: target_full: exact v0.2 documents encoded from raw pages

predictions_frozen_before_output.bf16: TA@10 = 1.0 (the 128-page Energy run already showed exact endpoint equality).
predictions_frozen_before_output.leverage: Qwen2-VL-2B has a 600M vision tower in front of a 1.5B decoder at 602k max pixels; leverage on document pages is predicted between 0.6 and 0.8, lower than ColQwen2.5 at 12.8M pixels.
predictions_frozen_before_output.quality: The earlier Energy result rejected PCA-256 (-0.027 nDCG@10). Prediction: PCA-256 fails the floor on at least one holdout while INT8 and PCA-512 pass on all three; if so ColQwen2 is a second positive backbone at a different frontier point.

claim_boundary: Second backbone, one release pair, one GPU, batch size 1. Same holdouts and split rule as the ColQwen2.5 run.
compatibility_baselines: Procrustes and affine ridge (lambda 0.01) bridges from target-version query tokens to legacy query tokens, fitted in-domain on the non-holdout 70% queries of the same corpus; evaluated against the legacy (stale) document bank. This removes the cross-domain (Energy-fitted) handicap of the paper's bridges.
